description: Correct DDD: three declared contexts (sales, billing, support) each keep their own model of the person they deal with: Customer, Payer, Requester. Billing translates the sales Customer into its Payer at the boundary (PayerTranslator, an anti-corruption translation). The model MAY say these are the same real-world party; the verdict must still be pass, because the rule only fires inside one context. This is the case the old case-03 would have punished.

ns02.layers: layers.json in this directory (declares the DDD contexts)

expectedFacts.subject: Customer
expectedFacts.note: either answer is acceptable; the verdict must not depend on it

expectedVerdicts.note: no two definers of one concept share a context

ns02.harnessStatus: Under the CURRENT pipeline this twin is a possible forbidden-hit (3 names in 3 components) if the model clusters them. Under the N4 rule it passes by construction. Reporting both is the point of the pair.
ns02.factPolarity: required: the run must produce it (agreed); forbidden: producing it is a false fact; tolerated: either answer, the verdict must not depend on it. Subjects are APG names (Class or Class.method), as in the mock-answer scripts.
